drug_class: Non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor (NNRTI) — a type of antiretroviral medication
purpose: Nevirapine is used to treat HIV infection in adults and children. It helps lower the amount of HIV virus in your body and keeps your immune system stronger. It is always used together with other HIV medicines, never on its own.
how_it_works: HIV needs a special tool called reverse transcriptase to make copies of itself inside your body. Nevirapine blocks that tool so the virus cannot reproduce as easily. This helps keep the virus under control, though it does not cure HIV completely.
common_side_effects: Skin rash is very common, especially in the first few weeks — let your doctor know right away if this happens. You may also notice nausea, tiredness, headache, or mild fever. Some people experience liver-related symptoms like yellowing of the skin or eyes, dark urine, or stomach pain.
warnings: Nevirapine can cause serious, life-threatening skin reactions and liver problems, especially in the first 18 weeks of treatment. Women with higher CD4 counts and men with very high CD4 counts are at greater risk for liver problems. Never stop or restart this medicine on your own without talking to your doctor, and go to the ER immediately if you develop a severe rash, blisters, or signs of liver trouble.
typical_dosing: Adults usually start with one 200 mg tablet once a day for the first 14 days — this is called the lead-in period to reduce the risk of rash. After that, the dose increases to 200 mg twice a day, or one 400 mg extended-release tablet once a day. Your doctor will decide the right dose for your child based on their weight and age.
